newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices ease, fear extra govt supplies.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices ease, fear extra govt supplies.

text.p: Sugar prices weakened in India amid speculation that the government will release extra supplies to the market, traders said.
Consumer demand and enquiries from retailers remained low while improved arrivals dragged prices downward.
"Arrivals remained higher amid increased offerings by the mill owners on fear that government may release extra free sale quota for the current month," one broker said.
"Free sale quota for the current month is 650,000 tonnes, while it was 800,000 tonnes last month," he said.

Meanwhile, ready delivery sugar S-30 fell by 15 rupees to 1,255/1,280 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 fell by 10 rupees to 1,290/1,370 rupees per quintal. Sugar mill delivery moved down from 1,200/1,220 rupees to 1,190/1,205 rupees per quintal on absence of fresh outstation buying at the mill level.
Overall sentiment was subdued at the close of the session.
